purpose: exportOutboxStatus was the only one of six exports with neither assertTenantScope nor a tenant predicate: it read outbox_entries across the whole table and returned full rows, payload and leaseToken included. The same pass removes the four .catch handlers that turned a failed query into a clean-looking artifact - an empty ledger CSV, a zero-operation regulatory filing, a deal report asserting chainIntegrity.valid on a database it never reached.
requiredInvariants: Role check stays first on every export, before the tenant check and before any read. The order is already asserted by the existing suite and must not move.

The tenant predicate is in the query, not in a comment and not delegated to RLS. Policy outbox_entries_worker_select is USING (current_user IN ('app_service','app_outbox')) and PostgreSQL ORs permissive policies, so under the service principal the database returns the table whole.
An outbox entry with no deal belongs to no tenant and is excluded. This is what the strict policy outbox_entries_select already does with "dealId" IS NOT NULL; no new semantics are invented.
No schema change, no migration, no RLS policy edit, no FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. deals_uncontexted_read and the move into RlsTransactionService are later steps of the chain and are not started here.
Nothing outside apps/api/src/modules/exports is touched. No production, REG.RU, DNS, database or credential mutation. New mandatory cost: 0 RUB.
acceptance: exportOutboxStatus refuses a caller with no tenant, like the other five, and the refusal happens before any read.
Entries are filtered by the deal ids of the caller's tenant; an entry whose deal belongs to another tenant, and an entry with dealId null, are both absent from counts and from the returned list.
payload and leaseToken are not selected. The returned shape is the explicit status field list already used by staff-workspace diagnostics.

Each of the four removed catch handlers has a test that fails if it is restored: a rejecting query must propagate, not yield an empty ledger CSV, a zero-operation regulatory report, a zero-count outbox status, or a deal report asserting chain integrity over a database it never read.
api typecheck exit 0 and the full @pc/api suite green.
